title: Give a second link its own multiplexer

blocks.text: The acquirer is adding a second network link. Its ChannelAdaptor descriptor is ready, and `LinkDescriptors.channelAdaptor(...)` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkDescriptors.java` builds it. Nobody has written the multiplexer that goes on top of it yet, and the operations team has three complaints about the last link someone set up by hand: requests timed out with the host up, the dashboard said "connected" during an outage, and messages from the host that nobody was waiting for ended up mixed with another link's.

Finish `muxFor(adaptor, muxName)` so that it returns the QMUX descriptor for the link that `adaptor` describes, as the `20_` file in `deploy/` would hold it. The adaptors in the tests use names and queues of their own, so read them from `adaptor` (`getAttributeValue`, `getChildText`). About 8 lines.
The tests deploy what you return as a real QMUX, put a stand-in for the adaptor on its queues, and send through it. A host behind the stand-in answers every request.

cases.says: a request sent through the new multiplexer reaches the host over the link's adaptor and its answer comes back
while the link has never connected, the multiplexer reports that it is not connected
the multiplexer reports connected while its own adaptor is connected, and not when only another link is
a message from the host that no request waits for is kept in a queue of this link's own

origin.section: 1.3 `isConnected()` Knows About the Link Only Through `<ready>`

concepts: The multiplexer writes requests to the queue the adaptor reads and reads the queue the adaptor writes; with the names copied instead of crossed, every request waits out its timeout and the host sees nothing.
isConnected() looks only for the ready entry named in <ready>, the adaptor's name plus .ready; without it a dead link reports connected.
